title: En la pista de baile
setting: Asking someone to dance at a Latin club in Ybor.

lines.en: Hi! Do you want to dance?
Sure, but don't step on me.
Relax, I'm learning.
It shows. Just kidding! You dance well.
Thanks. Where are you from?
I'm Dominican, from Santiago. And you?

lines.es: Soy de aquí, de Tampa. Estoy aprendiendo español.
lines.en: I'm from here, Tampa. I'm learning Spanish.
Really? You speak it really well.

lines.es: Poco a poco. ¿Te puedo invitar a un trago?
lines.en: Little by little. Can I buy you a drink?
Of course.

notes: "Dale" = sure / let's go. Super common in DR and Puerto Rico.

title: En el restaurante dominicano
setting: Ordering food and asking for the check.

lines.en: Hi, honey. What can I get you?
What do you recommend?

lines.es: El pollo guisado está buenísimo hoy.
lines.en: The stewed chicken is really good today.

lines.es: Perfecto. Un pollo guisado con arroz y habichuelas, por favor.
lines.en: Perfect. Stewed chicken with rice and beans, please.
And to drink?
An ice-cold beer.
Do you want tostones too?

lines.es: Sí, dale. ¿Me trae la cuenta cuando pueda?
lines.en: Yes, sure. Can you bring me the check when you can?
Of course. I'll bring it right now.

notes: "Mi amor" from a waitress is just friendly, not flirting. Very Caribbean.
"Habichuelas" = beans in DR and Puerto Rico (elsewhere "frijoles").
In the Caribbean "ahorita" means right now.

title: Textos después de la fiesta

lines.es: Hola, Yari. Soy Dan, el de la bachata.
lines.en: Hi Yari. It's Dan, the bachata guy.
Hahaha what's up. Did you get home okay last night?

lines.es: Sí, todo bien. La pasé súper bien contigo.
lines.en: Yes, all good. I had a great time with you.

lines.es: Yo también. Bailas mejor de lo que pensaba.
lines.en: Me too. You dance better than I thought.

lines.es: Jaja gracias. ¿Cuándo nos vemos otra vez?
lines.en: Haha thanks. When can we see each other again?

lines.es: Este sábado hay bachata en Ybor. ¿Vienes?
lines.en: This Saturday there's bachata in Ybor. Are you coming?
Of course! Let me know when you get there.
Sure. Kisses.

notes: "La pasé bien" = I had a good time.

title: En el gimnasio

lines.es: ¿Qué lo qué, mano? ¿Vas a usar esa máquina?
lines.en: What's up, bro? Are you going to use that machine?

lines.es: Sí, pero solo me quedan dos series.
lines.en: Yes, but I only have two sets left.
No problem. How long have you been working out?

lines.es: Como seis meses. Vengo todos los días después del trabajo.
lines.en: About six months. I come every day after work.

lines.es: Se ve. ¿Me ayudas con el banco?
lines.en: It shows. Can you spot me on the bench?
Sure, go ahead. How many are you going to do?

lines.es: Diez. Si no puedo, me ayudas.
lines.en: Ten. If I can't, help me.
Let's go!

notes: "Me quedan dos series" = I have two sets left (literally "two sets remain to me").
"¿Cuánto tiempo llevas + -ando?" = How long have you been ...-ing?

title: Conociendo a la familia
setting: Meeting her mom for the first time.

lines.en: Mom, this is Dan.
Nice to meet you, ma'am.
Welcome, dear. Sit down. Have you eaten yet?
Not yet, but it smells delicious.

lines.es: Hice sancocho. Aquí nadie se va con hambre.
lines.en: I made sancocho. Nobody leaves here hungry.
Delicious! Thanks for inviting me.
And you speak Spanish?

lines.es: Un poco. Estoy aprendiendo para hablar con ustedes.
lines.en: A little. I'm learning so I can talk with you all.

lines.es: Ay, qué lindo. Yari, este muchacho es un buen partido.
lines.en: Aw, how sweet. Yari, this guy is a good catch.

notes: Use "señora" and "usted" with her mom until she tells you otherwise.

title: En el Uber
setting: Riding to the club and chatting with the driver.

lines.en: Good evening. To Ybor?

lines.es: Sí, a la Séptima Avenida, por favor.
lines.en: Yes, to Seventh Avenue, please.
Going to the club?
Yes, there's bachata tonight.

lines.es: ¡Ay, qué bueno! Yo soy de Puerto Rico. Allá bailamos salsa.
lines.en: Oh, nice! I'm from Puerto Rico. Over there we dance salsa.
Can you drop me off at the corner?
Sure. Have a good time.
Thanks, you too.

title: En el colmado
setting: Buying ice and water at the corner store.

lines.en: Hi. Do you have ice?
Yes, my friend. How many bags?

lines.es: Dos, y un paquete de agua.
lines.en: Two, and a pack of water.
Anything else?
No, that's all. How much is it?
It's three hundred pesos.
Here you go.
Thanks. God bless you!

notes: "Buenas" is the all-purpose greeting: good morning / afternoon / evening.

title: Llegando tarde
setting: A phone call: you overslept and she is waiting.

lines.en: Where are you? I'm waiting for you.

lines.es: Perdón, me quedé dormido. Ya voy saliendo.
lines.en: Sorry, I overslept. I'm heading out now.
Seriously? You're always late.

lines.es: Lo sé, mi culpa. Llego en veinte minutos.
lines.en: I know, my bad. I'll be there in twenty minutes.

lines.es: Bueno, pero me debes un café.
lines.en: Okay, but you owe me a coffee.

lines.es: Te invito a lo que tú quieras.
lines.en: I'll treat you to whatever you want.
Hahaha, okay. Drive safe.

notes: "¿Dónde tú etá?" = ¿Dónde estás tú? with the Caribbean dropped s.
"Me quedé dormido" = I fell asleep / overslept.
